slides.title: VOLLEY
slides.speaker: Adityavardhan Mishra
slides.message: A Commanded Electromagnetic CubeSat Deployment Mechanism
bullets: Adityavardhan Mishra · Pratham Chawla
Symbiosis Institute of Technology, Pune

slides.caption: CAD-derived Blender rendering of the evaluated Gen5 assembly.
slides.notes: VOLLEY is a commanded electromagnetic CubeSat deployment mechanism. We developed and computationally evaluated a complete storage, transfer, launch and carrier-recovery reference. This presentation explains the engineering, the results and the programme it supports.

slides.title: The host moves the orbit. VOLLEY commands departure.
slides.speaker: Adityavardhan Mishra
slides.message: Add a controllable relative release state to a manoeuvring host.
bullets: Initial integration audience: orbital-transfer and rideshare host operators
POEM inspires reuse of an orbital platform; Electron Kick Stage inspires host manoeuvres
Individual departure velocity is an additional mission variable
slides.caption: Explanatory schematic. Release velocity and host velocity refer to the same event and frame.
slides.notes: A satellite inherits the host state and a relative release vector at separation. POEM demonstrated a powered, attitude-controlled platform using a spent PS4 stage. Electron’s Kick Stage demonstrated manoeuvres before satellite release. These are architectural precedents. Our evaluated host remains a generic manoeuvring reference, with no approved vehicle accommodation. The service question is whether additional local release control is worth its installed and operating burden.
sources: Blackbook §§1.1,2.2,8.1; ISRO POEM; Rocket Lab Kick Stage
slides.takeaway: Add a controllable relative release state to a manoeuvring host.

slides.title: The contribution is the integrated retained-carrier cycle
slides.speaker: Adityavardhan Mishra
slides.message: Connect custody, finite motor force, source response, arrest and mission burden.
bullets: Zhao et al. (2022): stacked electromagnetic deployment
Zhao et al. (2025): storage and transport interfaces; Feng et al. (2025): reachable-domain study
VOLLEY evaluates these coupled system questions for one explicit design
slides.notes: Adjustable electromagnetic separation is established prior art. We credit the published deployers and their experimental evidence. Our contribution is the design-specific integration and evaluation of a reusable retained-carrier architecture. The same represented geometry and mass connect the feeder, finite motor, source-limited shot, structural budget and mission comparison. Results from another apparatus support methods and comparisons; they are not measurements of VOLLEY.
slides.takeaway: Connect custody, finite motor force, source response, arrest and mission burden.

slides.title: A complete reference for twelve retained payloads
slides.speaker: Adityavardhan Mishra
slides.message: Define a repeatable path from storage to free departure.
bullets: Two fixed six-cell banks; one indexed captive pallet
Guided lead-screw feed; positive carrier capture
Reusable moving-magnet carrier; fixed three-phase stator
slides.caption: CAD-derived assembly view. The represented payload is a 3U envelope surrogate.
slides.notes: The academic reference holds twelve identical four-kilogram 3U surrogates. Their contact envelope is 340.5 by 100 by 100 millimetres. Two fixed six-cell banks feed one captive pallet on an indexed lift. The pallet docks to a retained magnetic carrier. The objectives are continuous custody, finite electromagnetic force, source-coupled release and arrest, and a mission assessment including retained resources. Mixed 1U/3U belongs to the subsequent prototype programme.
slides.takeaway: Define a repeatable path from storage to free departure.

slides.title: Feed one cell into a supported receiver
slides.speaker: Adityavardhan Mishra
slides.message: The selected guided lead screw transfers the payload into the lift-held pallet.
bullets: Index the receiver to the selected cell
Open the permitted restraint; advance the guided pusher
Establish receiving containment; retract the pusher and close the cell
slides.caption: CAD-derived operating sequence; display timing edited. Static fallback shown.
slides.notes: Follow the payload, not just the actuator. It begins retained in a fixed cell. The lift-held pallet is indexed to the source. A guided positive pusher advances the payload along the restrained path. The receiving end frames and keepers contain it before the pusher retracts and the source closes. The receiver then moves to the carrier. The lead screw offers controlled travel and a defined load path. Seven feeder alternatives were compared in Labs; their scores are engineering judgments, not measured reliability. We retained the runner-up and rejected concepts for traceability.
slides.takeaway: The selected guided lead screw transfers the payload into the lift-held pallet.

slides.title: Transfer custody before withdrawing support
slides.speaker: Adityavardhan Mishra
slides.message: One captive pallet stays with the reusable carrier through launch and recovery.
bullets: Carrier capture caps and independent pins engage
Keyed pallet shafts insert 12 mm and rotate 90°
Only then do lift grips retract and the lift clear the launch path
slides.caption: CAD-derived docking state. Modelled capture sequence; not a photographed hardware test.
slides.notes: Four pallet feet land on the carrier while the lift remains engaged. Capture caps, lock pins and the keyed pallet shafts establish carrier capture. Lift grips retract by 26 millimetres only after the permitted state is established. Before departure, fixed cams open the forekeepers. Electrical braking reduces the unilateral rear-contact reaction to zero; the payload then leaves. The pallet and magnetic carrier remain on the host, arrest under the motor map and return. This separates payload release from carrier recovery.
slides.takeaway: One captive pallet stays with the reusable carrier through launch and recovery.

slides.title: Finite geometry sets the motor force
slides.speaker: Adityavardhan Mishra
slides.message: Opposed permanent-magnet arrays exchange force with a fixed three-phase winding.
bullets: Integrate current density over the represented copper
Finite magnet blocks, active conductors and returns enter the calculation
Launch and arrest use their corresponding position-dependent maps
slides.caption: Local force/reaction schematic. The numerical model integrates the represented finite geometry.
slides.notes: The phased fixed winding and moving magnet arrays form a linear synchronous motor. Current density and magnetic field give longitudinal Lorentz force. The equal and opposite reaction acts on the moving array carrier. A periodic wave is useful for initial sizing, but finite end geometry and returns matter to launch and arrest. We report approximately 1.328 newtons per peak phase ampere for active conductors and 1.399 including represented returns. Pratham will now explain how those forces were coupled to a finite source and checked against the mechanical cycle.
slides.takeaway: Opposed permanent-magnet arrays exchange force with a fixed three-phase winding.

slides.title: Solve source, current and motion together
slides.speaker: Pratham Chawla
slides.message: The release event changes the mechanical connectivity of the model.
bullets: Phase voltage, current and back-emf
Finite capacitance and ESR constrain available terminal power
Rear contact reaches zero; the retained carrier then arrests
slides.caption: CAD-derived operating sequence; display timing edited. Static fallback shown.
slides.notes: The shot calculation couples current dynamics, finite force, source voltage and motion. The phase relation contains winding resistance, inductance and back-emf. The capacitor is not ideal: its internal voltage, ESR and physical power root are evaluated. Requested braking is also constrained by regenerative terminal voltage. Payload and carrier initially interact through compressive rear contact. That contact cannot pull the payload. After detachment, the reduced mechanical system changes and the same finite motor arrests the retained carrier. The audit checks the algebra and limiting logic of an instrumented production solver; it is not an unrelated full physics implementation.
slides.takeaway: The release event changes the mechanical connectivity of the model.

slides.title: The principal 3 m/s case completes release and arrest
slides.speaker: Pratham Chawla
slides.message: The six principal nominal/adverse and inductance cases pass their declared model checks.
slides.caption: Computed histories. Principal case: 3 m/s command, nominal source, 20 µH; source and case-specific checks apply.
slides.notes:
The source reference uses 64 Eaton-family cells in a 32-series two-parallel arrangement. Nominal capacitance is 6.25 farads and ESR 0.176 ohms; adverse source assumptions are separate. One three-half-bridge inverter uses ten MOSFETs per switch position, sixty in total. We show the nominal twenty-microhenry principal replay. Relative release is 2.999864 metres per second; stopping occurs at 1.507289 metres from the model origin. All six principal combinations of nominal/adverse conditions and three inductances pass declared checks in the refined audit. The 1 and 2 metre-per-second cases support the analysed range, while the full timestep audit applies specifically to 3 metres per second.

Displayed result context: 64 cells, 32S2P; 86.4 V initial source command; Principal nominal replay: 2.999864 m/s relative departure; Carrier stops at 1.507289 m, inside the post-release allocation
sources: Blackbook §§6.3–6.4; coupled shot and timestep audit
slides.takeaway: 3 m/s command → 2.999864 m/s release · carrier stop position 1.507289 m

slides.title: Check solids, states and the represented motion path
slides.speaker: Pratham Chawla
slides.message: Geometry is checked beyond a single assembly rendering.
bullets: Eight native and STEP states retain part identities and pallet counts
154 accepted sampled-motion and refinement checks
Named solid-volume mass ledger separates CAD material and allowances
slides.caption: CAD-derived launch-ready state. Native solid and exchange-geometry records support the displayed arrangement.
slides.notes: An isometric rendering explains the assembly, but geometric checks use individual shapes, connected-solid status and intersections. Eight states preserve the part identities and physical pallet count. The accepted motion record combines 135 retained poses and 19 final direct checks. Certain changes also have strict material-subset or conservative travel-envelope arguments. These are nominal geometric checks with stated allocations, not a measured manufacturing tolerance distribution. Represented dry CAD mass is 149.557 kilograms; a separate seven-kilogram power/control allowance is carried into mission accounting.
slides.takeaway: Geometry is checked beyond a single assembly rendering.

slides.title: Independent static calculations reproduce paired closure
slides.speaker: Pratham Chawla
slides.message: Use the same chassis, opposed loads and restraints for a meaningful solver comparison.
slides.caption: Computed bare-chassis comparison. ANSYS mesh refinement sensitivity is distinct from experimental accuracy.
slides.notes:
Magnetic attraction loads the carrier across the gap. The actual connected bare-chassis geometry is subjected to opposed inward patches with matched numerical restraints. Each resultant is approximately 3010.481 newtons. CalculiX gives 0.285983 millimetres paired closure; the primary ANSYS sample gives 0.286392, approximately 0.143 percent higher. Three ANSYS meshes examine refinement sensitivity. A sum of two remaining gaps does not establish each individual assembled gap. The individual-face budget additionally uses centring, flatness, assembly and thermal allocations. Solver agreement supports this matched numerical boundary; it does not measure complete assembled hardware.

Displayed result context: Each array patch receives approximately 3.010 kN inward; CalculiX reference paired closure: 0.285983 mm; Primary ANSYS sampled closure: 0.286392 mm
sources: Blackbook §7.2; corrected matched ANSYS static cross-check
slides.takeaway: Paired closure: 0.285983 mm (CalculiX) · 0.286392 mm (primary ANSYS sample)

slides.title: Thermal budgets and interlocks complete the operating boundary
slides.speaker: Pratham Chawla
slides.message: Electrical losses, contact assumptions and sequencing stay explicit.
bullets: Copper heating uses the current history and represented conductor field
Repeated-shot estimates distinguish bulk rise, local rise and cooling assumptions
24 nominal commands; 166 passing interlock-model tests
slides.caption: Computed principal-case energy account. Numerical residuals check conservation; they are not efficiency or reliability measurements.
slides.notes: Energy accounting includes mechanical change, copper, inverter, bank and auxiliary terms. Thermal estimates distinguish bulk temperature rise from local adiabatic observations. The 3.295053-kelvin quantity in the repeated-operation discussion is a temperature rise, not a percentage. Four hundred and fifty seconds is assumed shot spacing, not the diffusion time. The interlock model checks twenty-four nominal commands and one hundred and sixty-six tests, including declared power-loss, jam, disagreement, timeout and host-burn cases. These test the represented logic. They do not provide a measured probability of successful release.
sources: Blackbook §§5.4,7.6–7.7; source energy and interlock records
slides.takeaway: Electrical losses, contact assumptions and sequencing stay explicit.

slides.title: Compare equal delivery targets and count retained resources
slides.speaker: Pratham Chawla
slides.message: Commanded departure must earn its service value at the complete host-system boundary.
slides.caption: Selected feasible tested policies in the alternating target family with a 5 N host ceiling; device masses and burn guards retain their declared differences.
slides.notes:
A fair comparison includes device mass, changing host mass, recoil, fuel and allowed operations. We use the same target position and velocity states at a common terminal epoch. In the selected alternating-family five-newton cases, VOLLEY uses about 0.28987 kilograms of host propellant and ideal ground-pretrimmed springs about 0.05365. Retained device assumptions are 156.557 and 72 kilograms respectively. The result establishes no mass or fuel advantage for VOLLEY in this tested preplanned service. This identifies where a customer case must be stronger, such as a genuine need for on-orbit command flexibility. That flexibility has not itself been priced as demonstrated economic benefit. Native Orekit replay checks the declared mission arcs and J2 boundary; it is not a full flight safety analysis.

Displayed result context: Common payload manifest, target states and terminal epoch; Compare host-assisted VOLLEY with host-assisted spring alternatives; In the tested preplanned case, ideal ground pretrim uses less propellant
sources: Blackbook §§8.2–8.5; mission comparison and native Orekit replay
slides.takeaway: Host propellant: 0.2899 kg (VOLLEY) · 0.0536 kg (ideal ground-pretrim spring)

slides.title: A complete computational reference connects the machine to the mission
slides.speaker: Pratham Chawla
slides.message: The study delivers a defined operating cycle and configuration-specific engineering results.
bullets: Storage, feed, capture, departure, arrest and return are defined
Finite force, source response and retained mass are evaluated together
Geometry, structure, thermal budgets and mission resources share an evidence chain
slides.notes: The achieved result is a complete computational design reference. It provides an explicit payload path, a finite motor and source-coupled operating study, geometric and structural checks, thermal and control budgets, and a matched mission comparison. The 1–3 metre-per-second study supplies the evaluated academic envelope. The conclusions include both the supported operation and the system trade revealed by the mission case. This is the engineering basis for selecting and instrumenting a physical article.
slides.takeaway: The study delivers a defined operating cycle and configuration-specific engineering results.

slides.title: Development follows linked engineering questions
slides.speaker: Pratham Chawla
slides.message: Five-plus years of VOLLEY development produced a connected engineering record.
bullets: Concept and host architecture → feeder, carrier and finite motor models
Integrated computational reference → independent numerical comparisons
Reusable tools and Labs investigations → physical-development requirements
slides.notes: VOLLEY developed over more than five years. We describe the stages using the documented lineage rather than assigning every related repository the same age. Concept selection led to payload handling, finite motor geometry, coupled source and motion, structural and mission evaluations. The completed reference now supports prototype requirements. Related tools emerged from specific engineering needs. Adityavardhan will close by showing that ecosystem and its staged development direction.
sources: Blackbook development appendix; documented project history
slides.takeaway: Five-plus years of VOLLEY development produced a connected engineering record.

slides.title: An engineering ecosystem grew around the deployment problem
slides.speaker: Adityavardhan Mishra
slides.message: Each related project addresses a specific part of the development chain.
bullets: VOLLEY Labs: feeder alternatives, force benchmarking and new speed configurations
Reusable tools: motor design, separation/orbits, CAD automation and source traceability
GatewayCX: proposed cislunar network relationship; technical paper draft for future peer review
slides.notes: The ecosystem is organised by the questions it answers. Labs preserves mechanism alternatives, experimental comparisons, new speed configurations and lunar architecture studies. The related repositories extract reusable tools for motor design, separation dynamics, orbital comparison, CAD evidence and numerical traceability. GatewayCX is a separate cislunar communications architecture. Future VOLLEY delivery studies could consider deployment of suitable infrastructure for that network; no integrated flight system is claimed. The technical paper is planned as a publication of the checked study, with a venue still unselected.
sources: VOLLEY Labs research catalogue; engineering tool repositories; GatewayCX architecture

slides.title: Gen6 turns the reference into an instrumented hardware programme
slides.speaker: Adityavardhan Mishra
slides.message: Long-term cislunar delivery: 3.5 km/s departure research, with targeting and capture designed separately.
bullets: Gen6: instrumented feed/lock and motor/source articles, then a mixed 1U/3U prototype
Higher-speed programme: separate ~10 m/s computational design; 1 km/s stretch research objective
Future host: a POEM-inspired free-flying carrier, replenishable constellations and Artemis-era lunar science/communications
slides.notes: Gen6 begins with instrumented mechanism and motor articles and an integrated mixed one-unit/three-unit prototype. A separately specified Labs configuration has computed ten-metre-per-second release cases. Kilometre-per-second performance is a stretch research objective requiring a different source, stroke, loading and host architecture. The 3.5-kilometre-per-second case is a longer-term departure scenario, not an achieved launcher rating or automatic lunar-orbit delivery; lunar targeting and capture remain separate. The wider service hypothesis is standardised batches of short-life spacecraft, clustered or phased deployment, replenishment and planned disposal where mission needs permit. Artemis-era lunar infrastructure motivates later communications and science applications, including a possible GatewayCX relationship.
sources: Blackbook §11.2; Labs high-speed and lunar architecture studies; NASA lunar infrastructure programme
slides.takeaway: Long-term cislunar delivery: 3.5 km/s departure research, with targeting and capture designed separately.
